We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=9\sqrt{x} & \,⟹\,v=\int 9\sqrt{x}\,dx=6{x}^{3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}9\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(6{x}^{3/2}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{6{x}^{3/2}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})(6{({e}^{2})}^{3/2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡1(6(1)^{3/2})]-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}6\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{x}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =12{e}^{3}-(4{({e}^{2})}^{3/2}-4(1)^{3/2}) \\  & =12{e}^{3}-4{e}^{3}+4 \\  & =8{e}^{3}+4.\end{aligned}
$$
